historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly captures the two-state policy test but does not protect against testing the only admin path or confusing policy denial with network/credential failure.

original_test_intent: Verify that the BMC Shell via SSH policy is actually enforced for an approved test account: a fresh authenticated console session succeeds after enablement, a fresh connection is rejected specifically by policy after disablement, existing-session behavior matches the platform contract, and the original policy is restored without locking out management.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC firmware, management network, policy location and dedicated account/role; prove an independent WebUI/serial/physical recovery administrator; record original policy and active sessions; enable policy, wait for authoritative applied state, perform one fresh SSH login with trusted host key and execute a harmless identity command; close it; disable policy, wait for application, perform one bounded new connection and classify refusal/timeout/authentication response; observe separately whether any preexisting session persists; restore and verify original policy and recovery access while preserving security/audit logs.
manual_activity: An authorized operator controls the WebUI policy and independent recovery path, approves the test account and final state, and restores access if the SSH policy behaves unexpectedly.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware, management interface/IP and vendor policy semantics
Dedicated test account/role and harmless post-login command
Policy apply/propagation delay and enabled/disabled API/UI readback
Expected new-connection error class and existing-session behavior when disabled
Original/final policy, independent WebUI/serial recovery account/path and maximum attempt count
safety_requirements: Never use the only administrator or SSH path as the sole recovery mechanism
Verify independent management access before disabling policy
Use trusted host keys and protected credentials; never log passwords/private keys
Bound to one fresh login attempt per state and separate policy refusal from DNS/route/TCP/host-key/credential errors
Stop on wrong BMC, unexpected session termination/persistence, inability to restore or any broader access loss; no brute-force retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, account, original/final policy, error oracle, approval and recovery
Perform one secret-safe fresh SSH attempt per approved policy state and collect redacted transport/auth/audit evidence
Assist the WebUI change only after separate execution confirmation
Do not disable recovery controls, test other accounts, expose secrets, retry credentials, clear logs or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve account/role, apply timing, denial and existing-session oracle
Approve original/final policy and independent recovery
Review policy/SSH/audit evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The browser toggle plus SSH attempts match the source. It needs bounded fresh sessions, trusted identity and error-cause evidence; a generic login failure is not proof of policy enforcement.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use WebUI to apply each approved policy state, verify readback, then perform exactly one fresh trusted SSH attempt with the dedicated account and restore the original state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Enable, successful login, disable, brief apply wait, rejected login and 10/5-minute estimate remain; timing and error semantics are made explicit.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run a bounded two-state access matrix using fresh connections, policy readback, transport/authentication error classification and independent recovery, with separate observation of existing sessions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds dedicated identity, applied-state proof, precise denial oracle, session semantics, secret safety and restore verification.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: TCP timeout, wrong password, host-key failure or network outage cannot substitute for a policy-driven rejection; a preexisting session cannot prove new-login allowance.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Disabling SSH may terminate the control path or only block new sessions depending on implementation; management network faults can mimic enforcement.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must state whether disabling the policy should terminate existing sessions or only reject new connections and whether root/service accounts are governed identically. This test should use only the approved dedicated role unless a larger matrix is explicitly required.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT firmware, management path, policy semantics and dedicated account role
Original/enabled/disabled/restored UI/API policy state with applied timestamps
Enabled fresh SSH success, harmless identity output and clean close
Disabled fresh SSH failure classified by TCP/SSH/auth/policy evidence plus existing-session observation
Security/audit/SEL logs, independent recovery verification, final state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source coherently defines a two-state SSH policy matrix. Missing account, timing, denial cause and session semantics are supplyable prerequisites.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The access-control purpose is clear. Dedicated identity, recovery and policy/error oracle can be supplied, so execution remains approval-gated rather than blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2225 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00008-V002: approve the BMC/firmware and management interface, dedicated test account/role, harmless login command, BMC Shell policy applied-state readback and propagation delay, expected enabled success and disabled refusal/error classification, behavior of existing sessions, maximum attempts, original/final policy, secret/host-key requirements and independent WebUI/serial/physical recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents management lockout and false policy passes from unrelated login failures, while making fresh-session enforcement, existing-session behavior, audit and restoration traceable.
independent_technical_reasoning: An access-control test needs a controlled identity and a causal denial. A timeout may mean the service is disabled or the network is broken; an authentication failure may mean the password is wrong. Policy UI readback, TCP/SSH negotiation and BMC audit logs must be correlated. Existing connections often outlive a policy that blocks new sessions, so they must be evaluated separately. Independent recovery is required before disabling the same service used by the agent.
